body:
The PathPilot mill tool-table export format, from a real 770MX export (PathPilot, 2026-11-18). The file has 1002 lines: two header rows and one row per tool number 1-1000.

Row 1 (a marker PathPilot needs on import):
```
Mill Tool Table,<date and time> - v1,This must be the first row - do not edit
```
Row 2 (column names):
```
Tool number,Description,Z offset,Diameter,Z offset wear,Diameter wear,Max RPM
```
Rows 3+ (empty tools have an empty description and zeros):
```
1,endmill [1/8] 2FL R:0.000 loc:0.375 carbide dia:0.125 [37368],1.0000000,0.1250000,0.0000000,0.0000000,0.0
8,Slitting Saw [1/8] 30FL R:0.000 uncoated carbide dia:3.000 [34993],5.0000000,3.0000000,0.0000000,0.0000000,0.0
10,drill dia:0.500,2.0000000,0.5000000,0.0000000,0.0000000,0.0
99,,3.0000000,0.0000000,0.0000000,0.0000000,-2.0
```

Notes for the parser and the writer:
- Units are the machine's (inch here). Values have 7 decimals.
- The type, flutes, corner radius `R:`, length of cut `loc:`, material and Tormach part number `[nnnnn]` live only in the free-text Description (the PathPilot tool-description format). An import reads them from there when present and keeps the text as the tool's name.
- `Z offset` is the tool length offset; on many machines it is a placeholder until measured, so the import must not treat it as a stick-out.
- The probe (T99 here) has no description and a `Max RPM` of -2.0; a negative Max RPM is a marker, not a speed.
- A file from PathPilot's Import must keep row 1 exactly as shown.
